s: A pool of identical VMs that grows/shrinks on demand behind a load balancer - classic elastic web tier.
w: Launch templates define the machine image; the group maintains min/max bounds, replacing unhealthy instances and spreading across AZs. Scaling policies react to CPU, request count, or schedules; cooldown windows prevent thrash. New instances boot from the AMI, run userdata bootstrap, pass health checks, then receive traffic.
use: Steady-state web/API fleets with predictable scaling curves
Queue-driven batch workers scaling on backlog depth
Cost optimization: shrink overnight to minimum capacity
Immutable-infrastructure deploys: bake new AMI, roll the group
avoid: Sub-minute burst absorption - boot times lag spikes; pre-warm or use serverless
Pets with unique local state - treat cattle only

size.rps_per_instance: ~500 rps per mid-size VM (tune per app)

pat.d: Separate groups per workload class stop batch pressure from evicting API capacity.

pits: Scaling thrash on spiky metrics - use target-tracking with warm-up and cooldowns
AMI drift - rebuild images via pipeline (Packer) weekly or patch gaps grow
Deregistration delays cause 5xx during scale-in - wire LB deregistration with connection draining
tips: Compare to k8s honestly: fewer moving parts for simple fleets; no bin-packing or rich scheduling
